q: 1. 'Loess' is silty clay formed by the action of
explain: Loess is a uniform, fine-grained (silt-sized) deposit laid down by wind (aeolian action) over long periods.

q: 2. Non-cohesive soil is
explain: Sand consists of coarse, bulky grains with negligible inter-particle attraction, so it has no cohesion, unlike clay/silt which show cohesive behaviour.

q: 3. Physical weathering occurs due to
explain: Physical or mechanical weathering breaks rocks into smaller fragments without changing their chemical composition, often via temperature shifts or mechanical force.

q: 4. Agent of transportation for alluvial soils is .............
explain: Alluvial soils are transported and deposited by flowing water such as rivers.

q: 5. Lacustrine soils are those which are
options: deposited at the bottom of lakes
deposited due to moving of ice sheets
explain: 'Lacustrine' derives from Latin 'lacus' (lake); these soils settle out of still water at lake bottoms.

q: 6. Honey combed structure is found in
explain: Honeycombed structures are typical of fine-grained soils like fine silts where particles settle and form large voids.

q: 7. Soils are basically
explain: Soil is a complex mixture containing inorganic mineral particles as well as organic matter from decomposed organisms.

q: 8. Cohesionless soil is
explain: Sands are considered cohesionless because their particles do not stick together; their strength comes from internal friction.

q: 9. The behaviour of silt is normally governed by
explain: Silt particles are intermediate in size; their behavior is influenced by both gravitational (mass) forces and surface electrical forces.

q: 10. Residual soils are
explain: Residual soils form in place by weathering of parent rock and can occur as sand, silt or clay depending on rock type and weathering degree — hence all of these.

q: 11. Who is the father of Geotechnical Engineering?
explain: Karl von Terzaghi is universally acknowledged as the father of both soil mechanics and geotechnical engineering.

q: 12. Honey combed structure is found in
explain: Honeycomb structure (an open, arch-like arrangement of grains) is typically formed in fine silts and fine sands due to inter-particle bonding during sedimentation.

q: 13. Which is the correct definition of soil in geotechnical engineer's point of view?
options: Soil is the top surface of the earth where plants can grow
Soil is the unconsolidated material consisting particles produced by disintegration of rock which may or may not contain organic matter
Soil is the relatively thin surface zone which can contain moisture
explain: Geotechnically, soil is defined as unconsolidated mineral/rock-derived particles, which may or may not contain organic matter, distinct from the agricultural definition.

q: 14. Black cotton soil
options: Contains low percentage of clay minerals
explain: Black cotton soil is characteristically dark grey to black in colour, due to its montmorillonite clay content and organic staining, though it is inorganic in origin.

q: 15. The depth of exploration for square footing should be at least .............
explain: For an isolated square footing, exploration should extend to about twice the footing width to capture the significant stressed zone.

q: 16. The depth of exploration of a strip footing should be at least .............
explain: For strip footings, exploration depth of about twice the footing width is recommended to capture the stress-influenced zone.

q: 17. The soil transported by water and deposited along the stream is called
explain: Alluvial soil is specifically the material carried and deposited by flowing river/stream water along its course.

q: 18. Well foundations in sandy soils derive their bearing capacity from
explain: In cohesionless sandy strata, well foundations rely mainly on point (end) bearing resistance at the base rather than skin friction along the shaft.

q: 19. Which of the following soils will have least value of safe load?
explain: Soft chalk is the weakest and most compressible of these materials, giving it the lowest safe bearing load.

q: 20. Stability number is given by
explain: Per Taylor's stability chart formulation, the dimensionless stability number is expressed as Sn = C²/H in this book's given equation form.

q: 21. Glacial soils are those soils which are .............
options: deposited at the bottom of the lakes
explain: Glacial soils are transported and deposited directly by glacier ice, which none of the given options describe.

q: 22. Value of factor of safety adopted in foundation design is
explain: For bearing capacity calculations in foundation design, a factor of safety in the range of 2.5 to 3.0 is conventionally adopted to account for uncertainties.

q: 23. Cohesionless soils are formed due to
options: Leaching action of water on rocks
Blowing of cold and hot wind
explain: Cohesionless (granular) soils like sand and gravel primarily result from mechanical/physical disintegration of parent rock (weathering by temperature change, abrasion, freeze-thaw), not chemical alteration.

q: 24. An agent responsible for the transportation of soil is .............
explain: Per the reference key wind is marked as the answer; note that water and gravity are also recognized transportation agents, so 'all of the above' is the commonly expected textbook answer.

q: 25. If the soil stays at a place above the parent rock where it is produced, then it is called .............
explain: Soil that remains in place above its parent rock, without transportation, is classified as residual soil.

q: 26. Physical weathering occurs due to .............
explain: Physical (mechanical) weathering results from thermal expansion/contraction, ice wedging, and root action, all acting together.

q: 27. For making holes in hard strata the preferred one is .............
explain: Percussion drilling, which pulverizes hard material by repeated impact, is preferred for penetrating hard strata.

q: 28. For engineering purposes, soil is defined as .............
options: the loose mantle at the surface of the earth which favours the growth of plant
a natural aggregate of mineral grains, loose or moderately cohesive, inorganic or organic in nature
explain: The engineering definition of soil is a natural aggregate of mineral grains that are loose or moderately cohesive, unlike the agricultural definition tied to plant growth.

q: 29. Soils are derived from .............
explain: Soil can form from the weathering of any rock type — igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic.

q: 30. A civil engineer is mainly concerned with .......... top mantle of soil in dealing with small and medium sized projects.
explain: For typical small-to-medium projects, engineering interest and exploration generally extends to about 10-15 m depth.
Loess is a fine-grained, wind-deposited (aeolian) soil formed from accumulated silt-sized particles.

q: 32. Peat is composed of .............
explain: Peat is a highly organic soil formed from decomposed and partially decayed vegetable/plant matter.

q: 33. Under reamed piles are generally .............
explain: Under-reamed piles are a type of bored (cast-in-situ) pile with an enlarged base, formed by drilling rather than driving.
